test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 22 Aug 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Three statements are given, followed by two conclusions numbered I and II. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some beds are tables.

Some tables are cupboards.

Some cupboards are chairs.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some chairs are beds.

II. Some beds are cupboards.

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follow
Neither conclusion I nor II follows

solution:
Given Statements:

Some beds are tables.

Some tables are cupboards.

Some cupboards are chairs.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e6672ffe9ba96a665ca25597fff5f07c1e7acab7a9e5b9142d26dd7e710d02bf.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some chairs are beds - False (Because, No definite relation is given between chairs and beds, so some chairs are beds can be a possibility only).

II. Some beds are cupboards - False (Because, No definite relation is given between beds and cupboards, some beds are cupboards can be a possibility only)

So, Neither conclusion I nor II follow.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".
